turns.content: In triangle ABC with AB=AB, an altitude from A meets BC at D. Prove what this implies about the two base segments BD and DC.
Factor x^3-8x^2-8x-9 and identify the value of K suggested by the real linear factor.
Substitute that value into the original cubic, then use the remaining quadratic factor to show that no other real roots exist.
Set T=23 and BC=T-K. Use the value of K and the fact that D bisects BC to compute BC and BD.
The altitude KD has length sqrt(T). Form the right-triangle relation among AB, KD, and BD.
Substitute AD^2=T=23 and the calculated half-base BD into that relation, and simplify the resulting value of AB^2.
Use the fact that a side length is positive to take the appropriate square root and report AB in simplified exact form.
